marks.gloss_en: Rami bar Chama: the mishna implies that one who lifts a found item for another acquires it for the other
Rava: lifting solely for another does NOT acquire for him
candidate source 1: the opening clause -- but there each claims he lifted ALL of it himself
candidate source 2: the seemingly superfluous second clause -- but it was already assigned to buying-and-selling (2a.11)
candidate source 3: the all-vs-half clause -- but it is needed to teach that the half-claimant is a suspected schemer, not a returner of lost property
candidate source 4: the two-riders clause -- but it may be teaching that riding acquires
the surviving source: the when-they-admit clause must concern a found item, and its point is that joint lifting acquires for both
